subject: Post-call recap: NorthBridge inference SLOs & topology commitments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alyssa Park <alyssa.park@northbridge.ai>, Ethan Ross <ethan.ross@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: NorthBridge inference SLOs & topology commitments

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap from our call and clear next steps so we stay aligned.

Pain points we heard
- 99th percentile latency spikes during peak windows (currently ~800ms for conversational flows).
- Cost per 1M tokens is running above budget; model footprint and inefficient batching are contributing.
- Need predictable throughput for synchronous product flows (checkout chat + fraud signals) with bursts up to 5x baseline.
- Data residency / audit trail requirements: primary region us-west-2, with strict logging/retention for audit.

Goals you stated
- P99 user-facing latency target: <= 300ms for typical chat prompts (200-512 tokens).
- Steady-state throughput target: 250-350 reqs/s for tier-1 traffic, with headroom for 5x bursts.
- Keep marginal per-token cost under the threshold you shared (we'll map numbers in the attached matrix).

What we propose (high level)
- Immediate: run a focused load & latency test using your sample prompt set (Jasmine will coordinate).
- Short term: a Dedicated pool with quantized model variants + KV prefix caching to reduce per-token cost and improve p99.
- Fallbacks: multi-variant routing to cheaper model variants if capacity constrained, with automatic fallback to hosted capacity.

Action items
- Jasmine (SE) to send topology options + request list for test artifacts (sample traffic, auth for test harness) — due Wed 2027-03-03.
- Ben: send initial cost/throughput matrix (attached) and draft topology PDF by EOD tomorrow.
- Alyssa/Ethan: share example prompt corpus (anonymized) and confirm target test window.

Attachments: NB_SLO_Throughput_Model-matrix.xlsx

If that matches what you heard, we can schedule the technical deep-dive next week (60–90 min) to validate numbers and agree on a mutual action plan.

Regards,

Ben Carter

ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0112

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. This matches our view and a few clarifications from our side: 

- Production runs in AWS (us-west-2) and we prefer keeping the inference surface in that region.
- Traffic profile: steady baseline 70 reqs/s, spikes to ~350 reqs/s during business hours (09:00–18:00 PT), occasional peak events where we see 5x for ~20–40 minutes.
- Data/security note: we need audit logs and an SLA on log retention for 12 months (this influences whether we go Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).
- Models: primary model family is MPT-7B (we also run a smaller reranker flow using bert-base-derived models). We're open to quantized variants if quality holds.

Requested from Redwood prior to the deep-dive: an example load test harness (endpoint + instructions) and a preliminary capacity estimate for MPT-7B quantized vs a 13B alternative. Also, please include approximate cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted for the numbers you propose.

On the action items: we'll anonymize and share a 5000-prompt sample by EOD Wed. If possible, propose two slots for next week's technical deep-dive (one morning, one late afternoon PT).

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: NorthBridge inference SLOs & topology commitments

Appended the initial topology draft and a quick technical summary — see attached PDF (redwood-deploy-topology-draft.pdf). Key points from the technical readout:

Summary of technical approaches and preliminary estimates
- Serving topology: Dedicated A100/80GB pool for primary MPT-7B variant, with a smaller replica pool for quantized 4-bit variants to handle burst overflow. Autoscaling policy tuned for latency SLOs (scale by p95 queue depth).
- Quantization: int4 quantization with per-layer fusing where appropriate — estimated model sizes shrink ~3–4x, which drives cost down and improves cache residency.
- KV caching & prefix caching: expected to cut token generation by ~18–22% for common prompt prefixes (recommend a warm-up period during the load test).
- Multi-variant routing and graceful fallback: route to 4-bit variant when latency is within SLO, fallback to 8-bit hosted variant if Dedicated capacity maxes.

Preliminary numbers (ballpark, subject to test):
- MPT-7B (4-bit) on A100-80GB: p50 ~ 45–65ms, p95 ~ 85–130ms, p99 ~ 200–260ms for 256-token responses with batching tuned to average request concurrency. Estimated steady throughput per GPU ~1.2–1.8k tokens/s depending on batching.
- Llama-2-13B (baseline): expect p99 to increase 2–3x and require ~2x GPU capacity vs MPT-7B for equivalent latency.
- Cost: preliminary Dedicated runway shows ~20–35% lower marginal cost per token vs hosted for your workload shape when leveraging caching + quantization. We'll confirm with the test.

Next steps we need from you
- Share anonymized prompt corpus (you mentioned 5k prompts) + a few representative long prompts (400–800 tokens).
- Provide a short-lived test key or a proxy endpoint so we can run the harness in us-west-2.
- Confirm a 60–90 minute technical deep-dive slot next week (Jasmine to propose times).

Attachments: redwood-deploy-topology-draft.pdf
Related: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cNB_SLO_playbook

Thanks — Jasmine will lead the test orchestration.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks team — quick note from the SE side. I'm free Wed 2027-03-10 09:00–10:30 PT or Thu 2027-03-11 15:00–16:30 PT for the technical deep-dive; please let me know which works best.

A couple of clarifying technical asks so we can size the test environment properly:
- Do you prefer SAML-based auth for the test harness (we can support SAML/SOCS) or a scoped API key?
- Can you confirm the 99th percentile SLA target we should validate against (you said <=300ms, are we validating at 256-token median length or at a 512-token tail?).

If you confirm slots and give the sample prompts, I'll schedule the runs and drop a short pre-test checklist (instance types, firewall rules, and sample anonymization notes).
